item.title: Magician's End
item.description:
Raymond E. Feist

★ ★ ★ ★ ☆

As the culmination of a writing career spanning 30 years, this book does a wonderful job of wrapping up loose ends, and finishing the story. The matter of “finishing” any epic fantasy is always a difficult one, especially when the world has grown so large that a great many parts must necissarily be left out. But Magician’s End does manage to complete the Riftwar Cycle in the most satisfying way; the way a good stew and hearty bread fill you up so you know you’ve had a good meal. The immediate comparison for me is to The Wheel of Time, and while I believe WoT had the correct ending that it needed, it was not nearly as satisfying for the reader as the ending of Magician’s End. While WoT ends in a perfect neural way, one of my favorite facts about Feist’s writing shines through again; his ending is hopeful.

item.title: A Crown Imperiled
item.description:
Raymond E. Feist

★ ★ ★ ★ ★

Fantasy books that contain maps are good. Fantasy books that require maps are great! This one traipses all over Midkemia for good story-driven and story-advancing reasons. We learn about the Island of Snake (men), the Girdle of Kesh, Crydee and the Free Cities, then travel east to Krondor, Rillanon, and Roldem. After having read something like 15 books set in Midkemia, I have a mental map of Midkemia to rival what I could draw of the United States from memory, or even the lands of the Wheel of Time, a place where I adventured for 15 years. Getting to know a world at both the high level of maps and at the stories that occur within a single dot is wonderful.
